contentFull:
Light-based sensors target faster poultry quality control

A new €7 million pan-European project will test photonics-based sensors across the poultry chain, from feed safety to meat quality and by-product utilisation.

Tony McDougalFreelance journalist

Oct 17

News

Photonics-based sensors could help poultry producers monitor feed safety, meat quality and food traceability more quickly and precisely. Photo: Ronnald Hissink 

The European research project aims to give poultry producers faster, more precise information on quality, safety and traceability by introducing photonics-based sensing at key stages of the production chain.

The Sensor4Food project, coordinated by Turku University of Applied Sciences in Finland, will develop and test sensor technologies that use light at different wavelengths to measure properties that cannot be detected by the human eye. Six poultry-related use cases will be tested in Spain, Italy and Norway, covering stages from feed production to the final product and the utilisation of by-products.

A large and evolving sector

The project comes as Europe’s poultry sector continues to operate on a considerable scale. Annual EU poultry production exceeds 14.4 million tonnes, while consumption is forecast to rise from 24.2 kgs to 25.8 kgs per person by 2035.

The sector also represents a significant economic force. The poultry value chain provides an estimated 3.7 million direct and indirect jobs in Europe, supporting rural economies and export markets.

ALSO READ: Funding boost to tackle Salmonella in chickens

According to the project team, quality and safety monitoring can remain fragmented. On farms, producers monitor factors such as feed quality and rearing conditions and work to reduce stress to support bird welfare. Further along the chain, however, monitoring can rely on manual inspections, visual assessments and laboratory measurements, which can be time-consuming.

From feed safety to meat quality

Sensor4Food aims to investigate whether photonics can provide more immediate information. Potential applications include identifying harmful mycotoxins in feed, detecting pathogens and drug residues during production, assessing meat structure and identifying quality deviations, and monitoring protein products made from poultry by-products.

The project also plans to combine these measurements with data from other sensors and artificial intelligence-based platforms. The aim is to generate real-time information to support decision-making across the value chain.

“Real-time data available across the entire value chain enables faster, more accurate, and more resource-efficient decision-making at every stage of production,” said David Oliva, head of Cognitive Technologies at Turku University of Applied Sciences and the project’s principal investigator.

ALSO READ: Rabobank: Poultry markets face growing pains despite strong global growth

Potential beyond poultry

Although poultry will provide the test environment, the partners say the technology could subsequently be applied in other food and farming sectors, including pork, dairy and aquaculture.

“The poultry sector serves as an important and demanding test bed for the project, but our goal is to develop solutions that can later be widely applied throughout the entire food chain to improve product traceability and provide more accurate and real-time situational data for the various stages of production,” Oliva said.

European research consortium

Sensor4Food is funded through the European Union’s Horizon Europe programme and is scheduled to launch in September 2026, with a total budget of €7 million.

The consortium brings together 21 European organisations, including 7 research organisations, 9 small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), 4 large companies and poultry sector body AVEC, which represents 95% of EU poultry meat production.
translationZh:
一项新的700万欧元泛欧项目将在整个家禽产业链测试基于光子的传感器，从饲料安全到肉质及副产物利用。

该欧洲研究项目旨在通过在生产链关键环节引入基于光子的传感技术，为家禽生产者提供更快、更精准的品质、安全和可追溯性信息。

由芬兰图尔库应用科学大学协调的Sensor4Food项目将开发和测试使用不同波长光线测量人眼无法检测属性的传感器技术。六个家禽相关用例将在西班牙、意大利和挪威进行测试，涵盖从饲料生产到最终产品及副产物利用的各阶段。

**庞大且不断演进的产业**

该项目启动之际，欧洲家禽业仍保持可观规模。欧盟家禽年产量超过1440万吨，而人均消费量预计到2035年将从24.2公斤升至25.8公斤。

该行业也是重要的经济力量。家禽价值链在欧洲提供约370万个直接和间接就业岗位，支撑农村经济和出口市场。

另见：资助加码应对鸡沙门氏菌

据项目团队称，品质与安全监测仍可能呈碎片化。在农场，生产者监测饲料质量和饲养条件等因素，并努力减少应激以支持动物福利。然而在产业链更下游，监测可能依赖人工检查、视觉评估和实验室检测，耗时较长。

**从饲料安全到肉质**

Sensor4Food旨在研究光子学能否提供更即时的信息。潜在应用包括识别饲料中的有害霉菌毒素、在生产过程中检测病原体和药物残留、评估肉质结构并识别品质偏差，以及监测由家禽副产物制成的蛋白质产品。

项目还计划将这些测量与其他传感器数据和基于人工智能的平台相结合。目标是生成实时信息以支持全价值链决策。

“全价值链可用的实时数据使生产各阶段能够更快、更准确、更资源高效地决策，”图尔库应用科学大学认知技术负责人、项目首席研究员David Oliva表示。

另见：荷兰合作银行：尽管全球增长强劲，家禽市场面临成长阵痛

**家禽之外的潜力**

尽管家禽将提供测试环境，但合作伙伴表示该技术随后可应用于其他食品和农业领域，包括猪、奶业和水产。

“家禽业是该重要且要求苛刻的试验场，但我们的目标是开发后续可广泛应用于整个食品链的解决方案，以改善产品可追溯性，并为各生产阶段提供更准确、实时的态势数据，”Oliva说。

**欧洲研究联盟**

Sensor4Food由欧盟Horizon Europe计划资助，计划于2026年9月启动，总预算700万欧元。

该联盟汇集21个欧洲组织，包括7个研究机构、9家中小企业、4家大型企业以及代表欧盟95%禽肉产量的行业机构AVEC。
author: Tony McDougal
